The test image shows a ripe orange-red tomato fruit with large sunken, circular/concentric dark lesions (gray-black coloration with some white fungal growth). The lesions are depressed and show what appears to be dark sporulation. This is classic fruit rot pattern.

Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (sunken circular lesions on ripe tomato fruit), **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.

Let me view reference images one at a time.
Microscopy images for Rhizopus - not helpful for comparison. Let me check Anthracnose one more and Gray Mold.

I've used all 8 reference image views. Note: the test image Bugwood ID (5475189) is extremely close to the Anthracnose spore reference (5475194), suggesting they're from the same dataset submission.

**Summary of observations:**
- Test image: ripe orange tomato with large circular sunken lesions, dark gray/black sporulation, concentric ring pattern - classic fruit rot
- Anthracnose Bugwood_1: shows circular sunken lesions on ripe tomato fruit - best macroscopic match
- Alternaria references: all microscopy images (spores/conidiophores), no fruit-level match
- Rhizopus references: one wilted plant, one microscopy - no fruit-level match
- Anthracnose Bugwood_16: pepper fruit, different appearance

The concentric, sunken circular lesions with dark spore masses on a ripe tomato fruit is the hallmark presentation of Anthracnose (Colletotrichum species). The close Bugwood ID also supports this.
